title: Finitely many inseparable constant shifts of a polynomial with nonzero derivative
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $h\in F[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Suppose the formal derivative $h\prime$ [def-pc-separable-polynomial] is not the zero polynomial. Then the subset $B_h=\{b\in F: h(T)+b\text{ is not separable}\}$ of $F$ is finite. Here $b$ denotes the constant polynomial, and separable means coprime to the formal derivative [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. No valuation, infinitude, monicity, perfectness, or characteristic hypothesis is imposed on $F$ or $h$.

source.place: Agent-supplied finite-exception lemma using the coprime-to-derivative convention of Stacks Tag 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), lines 1164–1178, and the polynomial ideal argument preceding it in Tag 09H0 (fields-lemma-irreducible-polynomials), lines 1145–1150. The finite-exception assertion is not a separately numbered assertion of these tags; its intended factor-divisor argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Put $p=h\prime\ne0$ and let $D=\{d\in F[T]:d\text{ is monic and }d\mid p\}$. By [lem-trf-finite-monic-polynomial-divisors], $D$ is finite. Let $D_0$ be its subset consisting of the nonunits, so $D_0$ is finite too.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-exception lemma; derivative/separability convention from Tag 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), lines 1164–1178; polynomial ideal argument as in Tag 09H0 (fields-lemma-irreducible-polynomials), lines 1145–1150. The finite-exception result is not a numbered assertion of these tags.

proof.text: Fix $b\in B_h$ and write $f_b=h+b$. The coefficient formula for the derivative in [def-pc-separable-polynomial] gives $f_b\prime=h\prime=p$. Since $f_b$ is not separable, no polynomials $U,V$ satisfy $Uf_b+Vp=1$.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-exception lemma; derivative/separability convention from Tag 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), lines 1164–1178; polynomial ideal argument as in Tag 09H0 (fields-lemma-irreducible-polynomials), lines 1145–1150. The finite-exception result is not a numbered assertion of these tags.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid] to the ideal $I=(f_b,p)\subseteq F[T]$ and choose a generator $g$ with $I=(g)$. Membership $f_b,p\in(g)$ says that $g$ divides both polynomials. As $p\ne0$, $g\ne0$. If $g$ were a unit, then $1\in I$; but $I$ consists exactly of the sums $Uf_b+Vp$ (these sums form an ideal containing both generators), contrary to step 2. Thus $g$ is a nonzero nonunit common divisor.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-exception lemma; derivative/separability convention from Tag 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), lines 1164–1178; polynomial ideal argument as in Tag 09H0 (fields-lemma-irreducible-polynomials), lines 1145–1150. The finite-exception result is not a numbered assertion of these tags.

proof.text: Let $a\ne0$ be the leading coefficient of $g$ and set $d=a^{-1}g$. Multiplying every coefficient by the nonzero scalar $a^{-1}$ leaves its largest nonzero index unchanged and makes the leading coefficient $1$. Hence $d$ is monic. The equalities $g=ad$ and $d=a^{-1}g$ show that $d$ divides $f_b$ and $p$ and is still a nonunit: a unit inverse for $d$ would give one for $g$. Therefore $d\in D_0$ and $d\mid h+b$. This uses only coefficient scaling and the field inverses.

source.place: Agent proof of the finite-exception lemma; derivative/separability convention from Tag 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), lines 1164–1178; polynomial ideal argument as in Tag 09H0 (fields-lemma-irreducible-polynomials), lines 1145–1150. The finite-exception result is not a numbered assertion of these tags.

proof.text: For $d\in D_0$, put $E_d=\{b\in F:d\mid h+b\}$. If $b,c\in E_d$, subtract the two divisibilities to get $d\mid b-c$. If $b\ne c$, write $b-c=de$; multiplying by the constant $(b-c)^{-1}$ gives $1=d(e(b-c)^{-1})$, making $d$ a unit, a contradiction. Thus $b=c$, and $E_d$ has at most one element. Step 4 gives $B_h\subseteq\bigcup_{d\in D_0}E_d$. This is a finite union of sets with at most one element, so $B_h$ is finite.
